title: Review of c49's reacting thermals (fresh seeds 11, 12; g=0 twin, fuel fork, dt/2): Supported for S, I, M, D; E holds but by construction. Caps travel 3 sqrt(area) between birth and division in 9/20 and 18/21 dividing caps, and the fluid at each cap moves at the cap's own speed (ratio 1.02, same direction for every cap), so the cap is carried by its own vortex flow, not a burning front
summary: Fresh-seed labkit re-runs of the claimed world (seeds 11 and 12, 128^2, T=600, 1 t per frame), its g=0 twin (seed 11), the fuel fork at t=400 (seed 11) and the world step halved (dt 0.02, seed 11). Caps form from the random hot field and divide persistently: 29 and 33 persistent splits, generation 7 and 8, merge/split 0.17 and 0.20 (dt/2: 28, generation 6). c49's divmove.py: dividing caps travelling >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and their own division 9 of 20 and 18 of 21 (long axis 2/20, 5/21; dt/2 11/18), 37 of 41 upward, area jumps <= 1.5 in 40 of 41. My own check (advect.py): the heat-weighted fluid velocity over each dividing cap, from the vorticity channel, matches the cap's centroid velocity along its travel direction (median ratio 1.02 on both seeds, same sign on every cap), so the cap is advected by the flow it drives. g=0 twin: 10 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 of 5 dividing spots travel 3 lengths. Fork: components 28 -> 0 within 2 t (labkit components_final 0 vs 28 in the fed run). E holds but follows from construction (heat is made only by burning and decays).

verdicts.limitation: The direction of travel is set by uniform gravity; the thrust (buoyancy) is made by the cap's own heat and the cap is carried by its own vortex pair, which I count as self-propulsion along a fixed axis. Long-axis lengths pass far less often (7 of 41). E is by construction (heat exists only by burning). No resolution test (the world has no dx); 128^2 periodic only.
